narration.text: A black hole begins with a giant star, far heavier than our own. When its fuel runs out, the core collapses and the star explodes.
What is left is crushed into a space far smaller than a city. Its edge is the event horizon; past it, not even light escapes.
A star that drifts too close is stretched into a long thin stream. That gas swirls inward, glowing hot, in a bright spiral.
Most black holes weigh a few Suns, each left behind by a single star. At the heart of nearly every galaxy sits a supermassive one, millions of times heavier.
